clue.text: Well-mannered European admitting it

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A courteous continental traveller who is gracious enough to own up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' is a crossword favourite for a nationality; here it is a native of Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite is a direct synonym of well-mannered, describing courteous behaviour towards others.

clue.text: Upset some shopper, turbaned

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their letters is used, in an unbroken run

parts.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A shopper in a turban has been made unhappy about something.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to disturb or worry them, a verb synonym of upset.

clue.text: Distance in degrees outlined, shaped around Greenwich initially

indicators.note: something shaped has been moulded into a new form, so these letters are rearranged
the shaped letters are formed around the extra one, which joins the mix
initially points to the very first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the London borough

explanation.surface: Instructions for drawing something to a set angle, centred on the London observatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Greenwich is where longitude 0 runs, so the letter it supplies is apt as well as mechanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Longitude measures a position east or west of the prime meridian, stated as an angle in degrees.

clue.text: Short speech about bird of prey's claw

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A brief lecture on the hooked foot of an eagle or hawk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal but simply gives ON, placed after the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw on the foot of a raptor such as an eagle.

clue.text: Invites questions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: has someone round to one's home
second meaning: puts the same question again

explanation.walkthrough: Both words read as one invitation to put questions, but they are two separate meanings of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask someone over is to invite them round, and to ask over a point is to query it again.

clue.text: They mostly pick on us, running a place where free food is supplied

definitions.text: a place where free food is supplied

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move into a new order
mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A complaint about bullies, attached oddly to a description of a charity canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of the first word, then mix all the remaining letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: A soup kitchen is a charitable establishment serving meals at no charge to people in need.

clue.text: Song in second religious ceremony

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
pi is informal shorthand for pious

explanation.surface: A hymn sung during a follow-up church service.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword standby for religious.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiritual is a religious folk song originating among enslaved African Americans.

clue.text: Small containers — little girl's holding one

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Val, short for Valerie, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A young girl clutching one tiny bottle among her collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened name rather than a child: Val is short for Valerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Vials are small glass bottles used for medicines or samples, which are small containers.

clue.text: Give ground in retirement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to withdraw, as an army does
second meaning: a withdrawal or secluded place of rest

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an elderly person conceding a point; really a verb and a noun share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to fall back before an enemy, and a retreat is a withdrawal into seclusion.

clue.text: Cause resentment in joint after start of rehearsal

indicators.note: after places the joint behind the selected letter
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: An actor's twisted joint at the first rehearsal causes ill feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles keeps causing bitterness or irritation, so it causes resentment.

clue.text: Overjoyed, Bill mostly during jaunt abroad

indicators.note: during means within the span of something, so one piece sits inside the other
abroad means out of place, so the letters are scattered into a new order
mostly means not quite all, so the name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Bill is delighted to be on a trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten Bill, rearrange jaunt, and put the short name in the middle of the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Jubilant means triumphantly happy, a close synonym of overjoyed.

clue.text: League to hoist flag

parts.note: a union is a league or alliance
to jack something up is to hoist it

explanation.surface: An organisation running up its banner on a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The Union Jack is the national flag of the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union Jack is the common name for the British national ensign, a specific flag.

clue.text: Relatives and friends, scapegoats

explanation.surface: Family and friends being made to carry the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing things at a figure, hence anyone set up to be attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunt Sallies are easy targets of criticism or blame, much like scapegoats.

clue.text: Take legal action following one's publication

indicators.note: following places the legal action behind the other piece

parts.note: I is one, plus the possessive S
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Someone goes to court after their book is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is an edition of a magazine or newspaper, a single publication.

clue.text: Outspoken legal document shown in club, perhaps

parts.note: an instrument is a formal legal document such as a deed

explanation.surface: A frank legal paper produced at a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a members' venue, but it is the weapon defined by example, as 'perhaps' warns.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is one example of a blunt instrument, the heavy weapon of many detective stories.

clue.text: Study behind in mirror

parts.note: to take a subject is to study it
after means behind, as in following

explanation.surface: Examining one's backside in a looking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mirror' reads as a noun but is a verb: to copy or resemble.
explanation.definitionFit: To take after a parent is to resemble them, just as one thing mirrors another.

clue.text: Girl in Cuban city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a girl's name, as in the heroine of The Hunchback of Notre-Dame
second meaning: a municipality in Camagüey province, Cuba

explanation.walkthrough: The surface places a girl in a Cuban city; the girl's name and the city are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female given name and also the name of a town in central Cuba.

clue.text: Film theme skittishly altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the preceding letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A movie's main tune has been playfully changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skittishly' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; the signal is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sky's the Limit is the title of several films, including a 1943 Fred Astaire musical.

clue.text: TV detective's name — Garth? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means a little short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A quiz guess at the name of a television sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: Taggart was a long-running Scottish police drama set in Glasgow, named after its detective.
explanation.definitionFit: DCI Jim Taggart was the Glasgow detective in the ITV series that bore his name.

clue.text: Diet — it's about to make you most trim

indicators.note: about suggests turning around and around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert promising that dieting will give you the slimmest figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' suggests slim, but here it means neat and tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim can mean neat and orderly, so the most trim is the neatest of all.

clue.text: Cruelly hang leader of African country

indicators.note: cruelly suggests rough treatment, so the letters are knocked into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A demand to execute the brutal head of an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of African country' reads as a head of state, but the definition is just the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a country in West Africa, formerly the Gold Coast.

clue.text: Member going round US city in distress

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: an arm is a member, or limb

explanation.surface: A politician touring an American city in a state of upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a politician, but here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is fear or anxious concern, a noun synonym of distress.

clue.text: Left in danger, tragically, in St Petersburg some time ago

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: tragically suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned and in peril in the Russian city during its grim past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link, but belongs to the letters that get mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of St Petersburg was named Leningrad from 1924 to 1991, during the Soviet era.

clue.text: New book

definitions.meaning: first meaning: original, not seen before
second meaning: a long work of fiction

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a new title on the shelf, but each word is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel means fresh and original as an adjective, and a book-length fictional story as a noun.

clue.text: A racket, commotion echoing in slaughterhouse

parts.note: a racket is a type of bat

indicators.note: an echo sends a sound back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Loud noise reverberating around an abattoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' wants to mean noise, as in the surface; here it is a sports bat.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a place where animals are killed for meat, a French-derived word for slaughterhouse.

clue.text: Slender and elegant, the Parisian returned wearing new vest

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards
something worn is surrounded by the garment, so one piece goes inside the other
new means made afresh, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A slim, chic Frenchwoman back home in a new vest.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed French article sits in the middle of the rearranged garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte describes a figure that is slim and graceful, matching both parts of the definition.

clue.text: Tree is at the far side of park by river

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Directions to a tree standing at the end of a riverside park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means next to, placing the river first; the Tamar is an English river on the Devon–Cornwall border.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery shrub or small tree often grown by coasts and rivers.

clue.text: Plastic one inside works

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: a plant is a works or factory

explanation.surface: A single worker inside a factory making plastic goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like a noun for the material, but it is the adjective meaning mouldable.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic in its older sense means easily shaped or flexible, which is what pliant means.
